input.quote: 14.1 Indemnification by RevMed. RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees (\"Sanofi Indemnitees\") from and against any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement against any of them to the extent arising or resulting from:
input.rationale: RevMed's indemnity (14.1) covers its negligence/recklessness/willful misconduct, breach of its reps and warranties, and breach of its obligations (which captures the compliance-with-law covenant in 13.4(b)), and the procedure in 14.3 gives standard notice, control, participation, settlement-consent and cooperation mechanics; 14.5 also expressly preserves indemnity claims from the consequential-damages exclusion and there is no monetary cap, so no super-cap is needed. However, there is no third-party IP infringement limb. IP claims reach RevMed only indirectly via breach of the reps in 13.2, and the key patent non-infringement rep (13.2(f)) is knowledge-qualified and limited to the Development Candidate as at the Execution Date, while 13.5 disclaims any non-infringement warranty and 10.7 puts the first burden of taking a third-party licence on us. Conversely, our indemnity at 14.2(a) covers Third Party Claims arising from our Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products, so infringement exposure on the technology RevMed licensed to us sits with us. That fails the fallback, which requires a vendor IP indemnity as its material term. Minimal fix: add limb (d) to 14.1 covering infringement/misappropriation claims on the RevMed Licensed Technology, with the customary modification and combination exclusions, and conform the "(a) through (c)" cross-reference in the carve-out.

proposal.summary: Add a direct third-party IP infringement limb to RevMed's indemnity in Section 14.1, with customary modification/combination exclusions, and conform the carve-out cross-reference.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14.1 only reaches third-party IP claims indirectly, through breach of RevMed's (largely knowledge-qualified) IP representations, while Section 14.2(a) leaves us carrying infringement exposure from our Development and Commercialization of the licensed compound. We have added a direct infringement/misappropriation limb for the RevMed Licensed Technology, subject to the customary modification and combination exclusions, consistent with our position that the licensor defends IP claims on the technology it provides.

ops.text: (d) any Third Party Claim alleging that the RevMed Licensed Technology, or the Research, Development, Manufacture or Commercialization of SHP2 Inhibitors or Products in accordance with this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates any Patent Right or other intellectual property right of a Third Party, except to the extent such Third Party Claim arises or results from (i) any modification of the RevMed Licensed Technology made by or on behalf of Sanofi other than as contemplated by this Agreement or (ii) the combination of the RevMed Licensed Technology with any compound, product or technology not provided or specified by RevMed;
